cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-woven strip-woven cotton wrapper with indigo ikat blocks and warp-striping, explicitly attributed to Jula (Dyula) makers — a classic West African women's cloth type associated with this people.

physical.title: wrapper
physical.summary: Woman's wrapper; composed of thirteen narrow strips hand sewn together. Warp stripes in dark and mid indigo, red, yellow and white cotton with occasional supplementary weft float lozenge patterns in yellow and white cotton. Alternating with white strips with square blocks of solid indigo ikat patterning with fine checked patterns in white cotton. Cloth lined at both ends. Machine-sewn and embroidered hems at both ends.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-tailored strip-woven cotton smock with ikat-patterned and checked strips, a widespread traditional garment form across Mande-speaking peoples of the West African savanna including the Dyula (in Ghana/Côte d'Ivoire/Burkina Faso), consistent with the claimed ethnicity and region.

physical.title: smock
physical.summary: Smock made from a single cloth folded in two, with a hole cut for the head opening, and the sides below the armpits sewn together. The original cloth is of seven strips of machine-made cotton, the strips being of three different patterns using white, blue and red thread. Four strips have a pattern alternating rectangles of white cotton with blue ikat; two have a check of blue in warp and weft; and the seventh (placed in the centre) a different blue ikat pattern alternating with white rectangles with a red stripe running down the middle of the entire strip. The neck opening is lined with a dark factory made  blue denim material.

cultural.vision_reason: A handwoven strip-cloth woman's wrapper with indigo, white, red and yellow supplementary-weft float patterning, a style of narrow-strip weaving practiced by Dyula/Jula weavers across the Ghana–Côte d'Ivoire–Mali region; this is a typical example of such cloth used as women's dress.

physical.title: wrapper
physical.summary: Woman's wrapper (Suruku kawa); composed of thirteen narrow strips hand sewn together. Alternating warp strips: dark indigo with central white cotton stripe; decorated with supplementary weft float patterning in white and orange cotton. White cotton with dark indigo ikat blocks and central red stripe; decorated at regular intervals with supplementary weft float linear patterns in yellow cotton. Single red cotton strip at one side with narrow stripes in white, indigo and yellow cotton; decorated with supplementary weft float patterns  in white and orange cotton. Machine sewn hems at both ends.
